result.rationale: parseRefreshTokenResponse throws on failure but returns the raw safeParse wrapper `{success, data, error}` on success (lines: `return refreshTokenResponse;`). This is a real defect in this diff: in googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts the code does `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then `data: { key }` — storing the entire zod wrapper object (including `success`/`error` fields) as the credential key instead of `.data`, corrupting the saved credential. Other callers (office365, zoom) must also re-check `.success`/unwrap, confirming the leak

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/_utils/oauth/parseRefreshTokenResponse.ts`, the helper calls `schema.safeParse(...)`, throws when `!refreshTokenResponse.success`, but then returns the *safeParse result object* (`{ success, data, error }`) rather than returning the parsed `data`. This is verifiable: the function ends with `return refreshTokenResponse;`. Call sites in the diff show incorrect usage expecting parsed credentials, e.g. `googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` assigns `const key = parseRefreshTokenResponse(googleCredentials, googleCredentialSchema);` and then stores `key` into Prisma (`data: { key }`), which would persist the wrapper object instead of the credential payload. So the finding is grounded and indicates broken behavior introduced by this diff.
